newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka tea hauliers threaten strike.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka tea hauliers threaten strike.

text.p: Sri Lankan trucking firms which transport tea from up-country estates have threatened to strike if tea companies did not agree to increase freight rates, a newspaper reported on Wednesday.

The afternoon Observer said in a report that the Up-country District Tea Transporters Association of Sri Lanka was demanding a 40 percent increase in freight rates, failing which they would stop transporting tea from June 30.

The newspaper quoted an association spokesman as saying that hauliers were demanding an increase, the first since 1991, because cost of spare parts, fuel, tyres and crew wages had risen sharply in the past six years.
The spokesman said estate firms were making huge profits due to a rise in tea prices, but had declined to increase freight rates.
The newspaper did not say what the freight rates were at present.
Officials of tea companies were not immediately available for comment.
The newspaper said the association's 100 members plied 3,000 lorries daily for the tea firms.
Tea prices have risen this year on the back of brisk buying, mostly from traditional buyers like the Commonwealth of Independent States, the biggest buyer of Ceylon tea.
